title: Plate boundaries over time
description: Choose a boundary type and drag the time slider to watch plates move and landforms appear: ridges, trenches, volcanic arcs, mountains and faults.
simplifications: Schematic cross-sections: vertically exaggerated and not to scale. Real plates are 100–200 km thick and thousands of kilometres wide; real slabs dip at 30–90° depending on the place.
Features appear on a fixed, simplified timeline for each boundary type. Real boundaries evolve unevenly over tens of millions of years, and plates move only 2–10 cm per year.
The transform view is a map (looking down), not a cross-section. Magnetic stripes use a regular pattern; real reversals are irregular.
Continent–continent collision starts as ocean–continent subduction. Slab break-off is shown at a plausible time but is still debated for individual mountain belts.
